summary_paragraph: A 72-year-old woman with end-stage liver disease due to hepatitis C cirrhosis and a history of hepatocellular carcinoma was admitted in septic shock with altered mental status, hypotension, and pneumonia. She was found to have spontaneous bacterial peritonitis and Klebsiella bacteremia, requiring ICU care, pressors, and antibiotics. Her condition stabilized enough to undergo an urgent orthotopic liver transplant. Postoperatively, she experienced complications including fluid overload, pulmonary edema, and difficulty weaning from the ventilator, requiring re-intubation and aggressive diuresis. She also developed Enterococcus bacteremia, treated with vancomycin, and required a feeding tube for nutrition due to malnutrition and poor oral intake. Over a 23-day hospitalization, she gradually improved, was successfully extubated, and transitioned to oxygen support. She was discharged to extended care for rehabilitation, with stable mental status, functioning graft, and ongoing management of immunosuppression and infections.
